content.title: Texas Rangers 2026 watch guide: Broadcast options for regional and national games
content.text: This year’s Texas Rangers have range.On one end, Arlington’s ballclub boasts a rising star with 24-year-old Wyatt Langford, plus mid-20s talents such as Evan Carter, Jack Leiter and MacKenzie Gore. On the other end, the Rangers are relying on well-traveled 30-something veterans like Jacob deGrom, Nathan Eovaldi, Corey Seager and Brandon Nimmo. The front office made bold moves to acquire Gore and Nimmo. The window is open in what looks like a balanced American League.Texas has missed the playoffs in eight of the last nine seasons. The one exception is its 2023 World Series championship. Again, such range. What will it be this year?Intriguing as that journey sounds, keeping track of the weekly MLB slate can be a gauntlet. Blackouts complicate the regional access, while the league has added new national broadcasters in NBC and Netflix. ESPN is losing “Sunday Night Baseball” but gaining MLB.TV.There’s a lot going on, which is why we’ve put together this channel-by-channel Rangers guide. Fans should follow the team on The Athletic as well.You can watch MLB games live on Fubo (Stream Free Now!) all season.ABS is here - how will it affect MLB games this season?Joe CrisalliYour browser does not support the video tag.Rangers games on Rangers Sports NetworkIn-market fansThe Rangers’ TV territory comprises Texas, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Louisiana, plus the eastern portion of New Mexico. Most Rangers games fall on the club’s regional sports network, also known as an RSN. Texas’ is called Rangers Sports Network … yup, an RSN named RSN.Under current blackout rules, in-market Rangers fans can’t use MLB.TV to stream the RSN games live. Those with RSN in their TV package are all set. Those without it need the direct-to-consumer option, Victory+. Those who are still unsure can use this channel finder.Victory+ also has in-market access to the NHL’s Dallas Stars and to Texas high school football. Users who sign up by March 31 get $30 off and two tickets to a Rangers home game.Fortunately, select Rangers matchups are broadcast for free over the air. Here are the channel listings for major cities in the TV territory: Austin: KBVO Dallas/Fort Worth: CW33 El Paso: KTSM-Estrella Houston: CW39 Little Rock: CW Arkansas New Orleans: NOLA38-CW Oklahoma City: KAUT-CW33 San Antonio: KCWX2 Dave Raymond is Texas’ play-by-play voice for RSN. He used to call the in-state Houston Astros’ games from 2006-12. He has a fascinating backstory, too. As a reporter for Forbes back in 2000, Raymond uncovered financial fraud at MicroStrategy, a major dot-com bubble stock. As a minor league announcer, Raymond was part of a trade that involved crab cakes and a wind machine. Mike Bacsik and David Murphy join the ever-interesting Raymond for analysis.What you need to watch: A provider with Rangers Sports Network, or a subscription to Victory+ ($120 for the year until March 31, then bumps up to $150). Select games are free with a broadcast antenna.Out-of-market fansAll out-of-market supporters need MLB.TV for regional Rangers games.MLB season ticket holders get an automatic MLB.TV login code, and T-Mobile customers get it for free through their cell service. Returning MLB.TV subscribers keep their plans through the league. But because ESPN is now selling and running the package, all new sign-ups must come through ESPN Unlimited, with a one-month trial included for the newcomers. According to The Athletic’s Evan Drellich, users don’t need to keep the ESPN Unlimited plan to access the MLB.TV one, at least not for 2026.What you need to watch: MLB.TV. It’s $134.99 annually for ESPN Unlimited subscribers and $149.99 for others.Rangers games on national TVThe league’s national TV partners are sorted alphabetically, with the main days for MLB action listed below.ABC/ESPNMain days: Sunday for ABC, midweek for ESPNESPN and MLB have been tied together since the 1990 season. The stalwart is no longer home to “Sunday Night Baseball,” but its reworked agreement gives it 30 regular-season exclusives in 2026. That slate begins Wednesday, April 15.Over-the-air parent network ABC has three telecasts this year as part of the 30-game purchase.What you need to watch: ABC is free with an antenna. ABC and ESPN are included with most pay TV providers, and they’re also available with an ESPN Unlimited subscription (starting at $29.99/month). Some pay TV providers, like Fubo and a few others, include ESPN Unlimited with their subscription.Apple TVMain day: FridayThis is home to “Friday Night Baseball,” which started in 2022. That weekly window is usually a doubleheader, free from local blackouts but exclusive to Apple TV.The Rangers will host “Friday Night Baseball” on June 5 against the Cleveland Guardians.What you need to watch: An Apple TV subscription (starting at $12.99/month).Fox/FS1Main days: Saturday for Fox, midweek or Saturday for FS1, All-Star GameThere are 23 “Baseball Night in America” Saturday centerpieces lined up on Fox. The network airs two games at 7 p.m. ET and assigns markets by matchup relevance. For example, April 18 features the Rangers at the Seattle Mariners for those out west, while the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies draw an East Coast audience.Some Saturdays are doubleheaders with an FS1 game in the early afternoon. FS1 has an additional weekly spot falling on Mondays, Wednesdays or Thursdays. Fox and FS1 total more than 85 regular-season games this year.Come October, Fox has the NLDS and NLCS playoff series, plus the Fall Classic itself. Joe Davis has been on the World Series call since 2022, when he took over for longtime play-by-play voice Joe Buck. John Smoltz has been the color commentator since 2016. Fox’s World Series hold dates back to 2000 and runs through at least 2028.What you need to watch: Fox is free with an antenna. Fox and FS1 are included with most pay TV providers, and they also stream with a Fox One subscription (starting at $19.99/month).MLB NetworkMain days: Throughout the week Here’s our backstop, unassuming but reliable. The “MLB Network Showcase” has been around since 2009. The network usually airs a couple of games each week.What you need to watch: A pay TV provider with MLB Network, typically included in standard or sports plans. MLB Network also streams with an MLB.TV subscription (starting at $134.99/year).NBC/PeacockMain day: Sunday, Opening Day“Sunday Night Baseball” migrates from ESPN to NBC and Peacock, as the Universal network returns to live MLB coverage for the first time in 25 years. NBC, its streamer and the linear NBC Sports Network combine for 27 prime-time games and 34 afternoon ones in 2026. Some of the Sunday nighters are exclusive to Peacock.Texas makes its network reintroduction on June 14, parking the car at Harvard Yard to face the Boston Red Sox. The Rangers have earlier Peacock dates on May 3 (at Detroit Tigers) and May 24 (at Los Angeles Angels).NBC’s lineup launches with an Opening Day doubleheader on March 26 and concludes with the playoff wild-card series. To trumpet the return, the network has brought on some big names, including Bob Costas and Texas native Clayton Kershaw.Peacock usually has a live game in its “MLB Sunday Leadoff” spot, most of them with noon local starts.What you need to watch: NBC is free with an antenna, but Peacock requires a subscription (starting at $10.99/month for live sports). NBCSN is included in select pay TV providers.NetflixMain days: Opening Night, Home Run Derby, “Field of Dreams”Already venturing into live sports with NFL Christmas Day, Netflix has three MLB exclusives this season, starting with the 2026 opener (New York Yankees at San Francisco Giants) on March 25.July 13 is the Home Run Derby, airing with All-Star festivities. Aug. 13 is the “Field of Dreams” game, a neutral-site showcase in Iowa with the Philadelphia Phillies and Minnesota Twins. The Netflix arrangement runs through 2028.What you need to watch: A Netflix subscription (starting at $7.99/month).TBSMain day: TuesdayTBS Tuesdays continue in 2026. The Rangers don’t have any dates here through the first-half schedule, but that could change in July. TBS also has this year’s ALDS and ALCS playoff rounds … perhaps featuring your 2026 Rangers.What you need to watch: A pay TV provider with TBS, or an HBO Max subscription (starting at $10.99/month).Watching in person?
